title: What does UFO mean?
text: UFO stands for unidentified flying object. It describes something seen in the sky that observers haven’t identified.
source_title: U.S. National Archives — Project Blue Book

title: Where ‘flying saucer’ came from
text: In 1947, pilot Kenneth Arnold compared the motion of objects he saw to saucers skipping on water. Newspapers ran with ‘flying saucers.’
source_title: U.S. National Archives — Project Blue Book Anniversary

title: Explore NUFORC’s shape index
text: UFO reports come in many shapes. NUFORC’s archive includes triangles, cigars, orbs, disks, and even cubes.

title: The Al Taqaddum case
text: An object filmed over Iraq in 2017 puzzled observers. U.S. investigators later found it looked and moved like a cluster of balloons.

title: A little UFO history
text: The National UFO Reporting Center was founded in 1974.

title: Before online reporting
text: Before its website, NUFORC primarily received accounts by telephone and mail.

title: Project Blue Book
text: Project Blue Book received 12,618 UFO reports from 1947 to 1969. The U.S. Air Force classified 701 of them as unidentified.
source_title: U.S. National Archives — Project Blue Book

title: Why Venus stands out
text: Venus can outshine every object in our sky except the Sun and Moon. Look for it near sunrise or sunset.

title: How NASA studies UAP
text: UAP stands for unidentified anomalous phenomena. In 2023, a NASA study team published recommendations for investigating them.

title: NASA’s fireball cameras
text: A meteor that outshines Venus is called a fireball. NASA has a network of cameras to spot them.
